user_story: As an archive visitor, I want to browse records as cards in a multi-column masonry grid, so that I can scan many entries at once and pick one to open.
expected_behavior: On the default archive route the current page of filtered records renders as cards in a CSS columns layout: 1 column on mobile, 2 at md, 3 at xl, with break-inside-avoid so cards are not split. Each card shows a top accent bar colored by the hash of its first category (item.categories[0] or 'Uncategorized', indexed into the 6-entry COLORS palette), the publication (item.pub) uppercased, the date (item.date) in a monospace bordered chip, the title (with search highlighting), a summary preview (item.summaryPreview || item.summary || ''), and up to the first 2 categories as tag chips. Clicking anywhere on a card sets selectedRecordId and opens the record modal. Cards only render when not loading, not in error, and viewMode is 'grid'.
test_notes: Load default route (no hash). Observe the multi-column card grid; resize the window to confirm 1/2/3 column breakpoints. Click a card and confirm the record modal opens. Inspect a card's top bar color vs its first category.
notes: cards render in columns layout with accent bar, pub, date chip, title, summary, 2 tag/badge chip(s); click opens record modal.

user_story: As a curator, I want auto-submitted records that have not had a human review pass to be visibly flagged, so that I can spot entries that still need vetting.
expected_behavior: A card shows an amber 'needs review' chip (bg #fffbeb, text #b45309, title 'Auto-submitted; pending a human review pass') when recordNeedsReview(item) is true. recordNeedsReview returns true only when the record's needsReview field is boolean true or the string 'true' (trimmed, case-insensitive); every other value (false, '', a truthy non-true value, missing, null) is treated as not flagged. The chip appears alongside the category tag chips.
test_notes: If a flagged record exists in the data, find its card and confirm the amber 'needs review' chip is present with the hover title. With current production data no record is flagged, so normally no chip appears.
notes: recordNeedsReview only treats boolean true / string 'true' as flagged (verified in utils/needsReview.js). With current data no card in the default view shows the amber chip (0 present), matching the story's note that no production record is flagged. Chip markup + title attribute present in App.js card template.

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want to type keywords to find records by title, summary, or category, so that I can locate a piece I remember.
expected_behavior: The sidebar search input is bound to filters.search. Each keystroke updates filters.search and resets to page 1. Filtering matches the normalized query against a precomputed normalized blob of each record's title, summary (summaryPreview || summary), and categories joined by a U+0001 field separator, so a match must fall within a single field (a phrase cannot span title-end + summary-start). Normalization lowercases, NFKD-decomposes, folds typographic quotes/apostrophes/primes to ASCII ' , curly double quotes to ", en/em dash/bar to -, ellipsis to ..., drops combining diacritics, and collapses whitespace — so searching ASCII punctuation matches records stored with curly punctuation, and 'cafe' matches an accented 'cafe'. An empty/whitespace term matches all records. A helper line reads 'Searches titles, summaries, and categories'. Searching while on the folders route auto-navigates back to the archive (cards) route.
test_notes: Type a known title fragment in the sidebar search; confirm matching cards appear and the results count updates. Try a title that contains a curly apostrophe/dash using straight ASCII punctuation and confirm it still matches. Search while in folder view and confirm it switches to card view.
notes: keyword search filters (all=26615 -> "press"=23511); ASCII apostrophe "rosen's" returned 74 results (normalization active); helper line present; searching from folders bounced back to archive (onFolders before=true).

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want my search term highlighted in card titles and summaries, so that I can see why a record matched.
expected_behavior: Card titles and summary previews wrap text in a Highlight component that, when filters.search is at least 2 characters, splits on a case-insensitive regex of the (regex-escaped) term and wraps matches in <mark>. With a term shorter than 2 characters (or empty) the text renders unhighlighted. Note: highlighting matches the raw typed term against the raw (un-normalized) display text, so a record that matched via normalization (e.g. typed straight quote vs stored curly quote) may show no highlight even though it appears in results.
test_notes: Search a 2+ char term that appears literally in a title; confirm the matched substring is highlighted. Search a term that only matches via punctuation normalization (straight quote vs curly) and observe the card appears but the term is not visibly marked.
code_smell: Highlight uses the raw search term against raw text while filtering uses normalized text, so normalized-only matches surface in results with no visible highlight.
notes: 2+ char term "press" produced 9 <mark> highlights; single char "p" produced 0 (no highlight, as designed). SMELL is real but cosmetic per code (Highlight matches raw term against raw text while filter uses normalized text) — a normalized-only match would surface unhighlighted; does not break search.

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want suggestions as I type in the search box, so that I can pick a known term without typing it fully.
expected_behavior: When the search input has more than 1 character, suggestions appear: the autocompleteIndex terms whose normalized form contains the normalized typed value, capped at the first 8, shown in a dropdown. Clicking a suggestion sets filters.search to that exact term and closes the dropdown. Re-focusing the input re-opens suggestions only if the current value length is greater than 1. Clicking outside the search container (mousedown) closes the dropdown. With 1 or fewer characters the dropdown is hidden; with more than 1 char but zero matches the dropdown does not render (showSuggestions true but suggestions.length is 0).
test_notes: Type 2+ characters of a common term; confirm up to 8 suggestions appear. Click one and confirm the search fills and results filter. Click elsewhere on the page and confirm the dropdown closes. Type a 2-char string with no matches and confirm no dropdown.
notes: "jo" showed 8 suggestions (<=8); clicking first set search to ""#journalism says it’s time to quit journalism..." is not a good summary of...". 1-char "j" hid dropdown; 2-char no-match "zzqx" rendered no dropdown.

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want a one-click way to clear my search, so that I can reset the keyword filter without selecting and deleting text.
expected_behavior: When filters.search is non-empty an XCircle button appears inside the search input (right side). Clicking it sets filters.search to '' (clearing only the search filter, leaving other filters intact). The button is absent when the search is empty.
test_notes: Type into the search box, confirm the clear (x) icon appears, click it, and confirm only the search text clears while category/era/type selections remain.
notes: clear (x) button present while search non-empty; clicking it emptied the search and left 1 category filter(s) intact.

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want to filter records by one or more thematic categories, so that I can narrow the archive to topics I care about.
expected_behavior: The sidebar lists category checkboxes from facets.categories, initially showing the first 10. Toggling a checkbox adds/removes that category from filters.categories. Multiple selected categories are combined with AND: a record must include every selected category (filters.categories.every(cat => r.categories.includes(cat))). Selecting filters resets to page 1. When more than 10 categories exist a 'View All (N more)' / 'View Less' toggle expands or collapses the full list.
test_notes: Check one category and confirm the result count drops and only matching cards show. Check a second category and confirm results require both (AND). Click 'View All' to reveal the rest of the categories, then 'View Less'.
notes: category "Audience & Public Engagement" narrowed 26615 -> 3744; adding a 2nd category combined with AND (94 <= 3744). 6 categories (<=10) so no View All/Less toggle renders (correct).

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want to filter records to a named era, so that I can focus on a period of Jay Rosen's work.
expected_behavior: The sidebar Timeline section shows an 'All eras' radio plus one radio per facets.eras entry. Selecting an era sets filters.era and clears filters.year (era and exact-year are mutually exclusive). Selecting the same era again via handleEraChange toggles it back to null. 'All eras' is checked only when both era and year are null and clears both. Year takes precedence over era in filtering: if filters.year is set, records are matched by exact year and era is ignored; otherwise records match by r.era === filters.era. A helper line notes you can filter by era or click a year in the timeline bar.
test_notes: Pick an era radio; confirm results narrow to that era and the timeline year filter (if any) clears. Pick 'All eras' to reset. Note re-clicking the same era via the radio re-selects it (radios do not fire onChange when already checked).
notes: era "Public Journalism (90s)" narrowed 26615 -> 66; "All eras" restored 26615. Era/year mutual exclusion enforced in handleEraChange/handleYearSelect (verified in source).

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want to filter by content type (articles, Twitter/X, Bluesky), so that I can separate long-form work from social posts.

Any non-null, non-'article' value keeps only social records, then for 'twitter' keeps only records whose pub includes 'twitter' or 'x.com' (case-insensitive) and for 'bluesky' keeps only records whose pub includes 'bluesky'. Selecting a type resets to page 1.
test_notes: Select 'Articles' and confirm social posts disappear. Select 'Twitter/X' and 'Bluesky' and confirm only matching social posts remain. Confirm 'All' restores everything.
notes: Articles=950 (< all 26615, excludes social); Twitter/X=22507; Bluesky=2677; All restored 26615.

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want to clear every filter at once, so that I can start a fresh browse without unchecking each control.
expected_behavior: The sidebar 'Reset all filters' button and the empty-state 'Clear all filters' button both set filters back to { search: '', categories: [], era: null, year: null, publication: [], type: null, includeReplies: false }, restoring the full archive and resetting to page 1.
test_notes: Apply several filters, click 'Reset all filters' in the sidebar, confirm all controls clear and the full record count returns. Repeat with the 'Clear all filters' button shown in the no-results state.

user_story: As a mobile visitor, I want filters in a slide-out drawer, so that I can filter without the sidebar taking up the small screen.

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want to sort records by date or title, so that I can read in chronological or alphabetical order.
expected_behavior: A sort <select> offers 'Newest first' (date-desc), 'Oldest first' (date-asc), 'Title (A-Z)' (title-asc). date-asc sorts by a.date.localeCompare, title-asc by a.title.localeCompare, and any other value (date-desc) by b.date.localeCompare (descending). Changing sort resets to page 1. The initial sortBy state is 'date-asc' (oldest first), even though the dropdown lists 'Newest first' first.
test_notes: Open the Sort dropdown, switch between the three options, and confirm card order changes accordingly. Note the page initially loads in 'Oldest first' order despite 'Newest first' being the top option.
code_smell: Default sortBy is 'date-asc' (oldest first) but the dropdown's first/visually-default option is 'Newest first' (date-desc); the rendered select value still reflects date-asc, so initial order may surprise users expecting newest first.

SMELL confirmed but cosmetic: default value is date-asc (oldest) while the first/visually-default option is "Newest first" (date-desc) — the select correctly renders date-asc, so the dropdown label and actual order are consistent; only the option ORDER may mislead. First cards dated 1986-01-01, 1989-01-01, 1989-02-03.

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want to see how many records match my current filters, so that I know how much I'm browsing.
expected_behavior: Above the grid a line reads 'Loading archive...' while loading, otherwise '{filteredRecords.length} records found'. Controls render only in grid view, when not loading, and when totalPages > 1: a Prev (ChevronLeft) button, 'Page X of Y' text, and a Next (ChevronRight) button. Clicking a folder sets filters.categories to just that category and navigates to the archive (cards) route. The Cards/Folders toggle in the tools bar switches routes. test_notes: Switch to Folders via the toggle. Confirm at most 6 folder tiles for categories with 10+ records, sorted by count. Click a folder and confirm it switches to cards filtered to that category. From folders, type a search and confirm it bounces back to cards.

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want a clear message when nothing matches my filters, so that I know to adjust them.

This is gated on grid view (the archive grid block).

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want feedback while the archive loads and a clear recovery path if it fails, so that I'm not left staring at a blank page.
expected_behavior: On the archive/entities routes the ~13MB core data is fetched once (gated by a ref; the analytics route is skipped because it draws from prebuilt aggregates, and navigating away from analytics back-fills the data). While loading, the grid area shows a LoadingQuotes component and the count reads 'Loading archive...'. On fetch failure, error is set to a friendly message and a red error panel (AlertCircle, 'Error loading archive', message, 'Reload Page' button that calls window.location.reload) renders on both the archive grid and the entity browser, so the entity route never shows an empty browser with no explanation. After load, preloadDetails() is scheduled ~1s later.
test_notes: On a fresh load watch the loading quotes and 'Loading archive...'. To exercise the error path, block/break the core-data fetch (e.g. offline or rename the data file) and confirm the red error panel with a working Reload button on both the archive and #entities routes.
notes: aborting the core-data fetch surfaced the red "Error loading archive" panel with a "Reload Page" button on the archive route, and the same panel on #entities (shared fail-loud per #369). Loading state ("Loading archive..." + LoadingQuotes) confirmed during normal cold loads.

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want a visual histogram of records by year, so that I can see the archive's distribution over time and jump to a year.
expected_behavior: On the archive route (hidden once a search or era filter or year is active — it only shows when no search, no era, and no category are set) the Timeline renders one bar per year across [minYear-1 .. maxYear+1] of parsable record years. Bar height is log-scaled (Math.log(count+1)/logMax * 100, min 8% for nonzero counts; zero-count years render no bar). Hovering a bar shows a tooltip with the year and '{count} records'. Year labels show on multiples of 5 plus the first and last year. Clicking a bar sets filters.year to that year (clearing era) and toggles off if the same year is clicked again. The selected year's bar is highlighted with a dot marker. A collapse/expand chevron hides/shows the bar area; the header shows the year range chip. If no records have parsable years the timeline returns null (renders nothing).

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want a visible indicator and one-click clear when a specific year is selected, so that I can undo a year filter quickly.
expected_behavior: When filters.year is set, the Timeline header shows a red 'Clear filter (YEAR)' button that calls onSelectYear(null), clearing the year filter. Selecting a year sets filters.year and clears filters.era (handleYearSelect). Filtering by exact year (when set) takes precedence over era filtering.
test_notes: Click a timeline year, confirm the red 'Clear filter (year)' button appears in the timeline header, click it, and confirm the year filter clears and all years return.

expected_behavior: On the default archive route (only when not loading and no search, era, year, or category filter is active) a Featured Works section shows 3 of the 20 FEATURED_WORKS as external-link cards (target _blank), each with a type icon/badge, image (grayscale, colorizing on hover), title, an 'Explore' affordance, and a hover tooltip with the description (hidden below sm). A header chevron collapses/expands the whole section (collapsing also stops rotation and hides the dots).

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want to open a record in a modal and step to the previous/next record, so that I can read full details and move through results without returning to the grid.

Selecting a record updates the URL ?record=ID via history.replaceState; clearing it removes the param.

Visit ?record=RECORD-00001 directly and confirm the modal opens on load; visit ?record=BADID and confirm no modal renders.

Deep link ?record=dissertation-1986 opened the modal on cold load; ?record=BADID-NONEXISTENT rendered no modal (isOpen true but record null).

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want to click a category or term inside a record and have the archive filter to it, so that I can pivot from one record to related ones.

Search-term drill-down (onFilterSearch) confirmed separately in-browser: clicking a modal Tag set the archive search box to that term and stayed on the archive route.

feature: Hash routing and legacy URL migration
user_story: As an archive visitor, I want shareable URLs for each view and old links to keep working, so that bookmarks and shared links land me in the right place.
expected_behavior: The app derives the current route from the hash (default archive, #folders, #entities, #dissertation, #about, #analytics) and re-syncs on hashchange and popstate. On mount it migrates legacy ?view= URLs. The dissertation, about, and analytics routes render full-page components with a back-to-archive control. ?record=ID is initialized from the URL on mount and validated once records load (cleared if no record matches). Full-page routes (dissertation/about/analytics) return early before the grid chrome renders.
test_notes: Change the hash to #folders, #entities, #dissertation, #about, #analytics and confirm each view loads; use browser back/forward and confirm the view follows. Load a legacy ?view= URL and confirm it migrates. Deep-link ?record=ID on #entities and confirm the record modal opens over the entity browser.
notes: all hash routes load and survive the hashchange/popstate sync: {"folders":true,"entities":true,"dissertation":true,"about":true,"analytics":true}; legacy ?view=dissertation migrated to #dissertation. Note: migrateLegacyUrl (router.js) only maps ?view=dissertation and ?view=about — ?view=entities/folders/analytics are NOT migrated (migratedEntities=false); harmless since those are the only legacy URLs that existed, but the story's "migrates legacy ?view= URLs" is narrower than it sounds.

Open the tools modal via 'More' (and the mobile Compass). Click 'Report a bug' and confirm the bug-report flow opens. Scroll and confirm the header gains a shadow.
notes: header has logo, Report-a-bug button; inline Tools bar shows Mind Map / Entities / Analytics / More; Mind Map routed to #dissertation; header gained shadow after scrolling past 10px.

user_story: As an archive visitor, I want footer links to every major view, so that I can navigate from the bottom of a long page.
expected_behavior: The footer shows an archive blurb, an Explore column with buttons routing to archive, dissertation mind map, entity browser, analytics dashboard, and about, and a Credits column with the curator GitHub link and the record count / year range.
test_notes: Scroll to the footer and click each Explore link, confirming it routes to the matching view. Confirm the Credits show the record total and year span.

user_story: As an archive visitor scrolling a long grid, I want a back-to-top button, so that I can return to the header without manual scrolling.
expected_behavior: A floating ChevronUp button (bottom-right, fixed) appears once window.scrollY exceeds 500 and smooth-scrolls to top when clicked. It is hidden near the top of the page.
test_notes: Scroll down more than ~500px and confirm the back-to-top button appears bottom-right; click it and confirm a smooth scroll to the top, then confirm the button hides again near the top.

user_story: As a reader, I want to click a record and see its full detail in a modal, so that I can read the summary, quote, and metadata without leaving the grid.
expected_behavior: When isOpen and a record are present, a centered dialog (role=dialog, aria-modal=true, z-[80]) renders over a blurred dark backdrop. body scroll is locked (document.body.style.overflow='hidden') on open and restored on close/unmount. The header shows date, a type label (Video if url contains youtube/vimeo, else the social pub or 'Social Media' for type==='social', 'Dissertation' for type==='Dissertation', otherwise 'Article'), title, author (defaults to 'Jay Rosen' if missing), and an external 'Read on <pub>' link only when url exists and is not '#'. Footer shows 'N of total' (hidden on mobile) and Previous/Next buttons. If !isOpen or !record, renders null.
test_notes: Click any card in the archive grid. Confirm the modal opens, body behind it does not scroll, and the header/type label match the record. Close and confirm page scroll returns.
code_smell: isVideo/youtubeId are recomputed on every render; type label string logic is duplicated inline and hard to test in isolation.
notes: role=dialog aria-modal=true, z=80, body overflow="hidden", backdrop=true, title="The Impossible Press: American Journalis". Smell (recomputed isVideo/youtubeId, duplicated type-label string) is a perf/testability nit, not a behavior bug — confirmed render is correct.

user_story: As a reader, I want the heavy details (summary, quote, concepts, related ids) fetched only when I open a record, so that the grid stays fast.
expected_behavior: On open, if the record already has summary and url it is used directly (no fetch). Otherwise loadingDetails=true, a 'Loading...' chip with a spinning Loader2 appears in the header, and fetchRecordDetails(record.id) runs. On success the result is merged ({...record, ...details}). On a falsy result a fallback record is built from summaryPreview||title, empty quote/concepts/tags, url='#', author=record.author||'Jay Rosen', relatedIds=[]. Display always uses fullRecord||record. The effect re-runs on record.id change.
test_notes: Open a card whose detail isn't preloaded (cold load) and watch for the 'Loading...' chip, then the summary/quote/tags appearing. Open a record id known to have no details row to confirm the fallback renders title as summary.
code_smell: The fetch effect has no error/catch branch — a rejected fetchRecordDetails promise leaves loadingDetails stuck true. The merge {...record, ...details} can let stale detail fields override fresh core fields (the needsReview comment calls this out).
notes: Details resolved (not stuck loading) and summary/thread body rendered=true. SMELL CONFIRMED by code inspection: the fetch effect (RecordModal.js:66) has .then() but NO .catch() — a rejected fetchRecordDetails leaves loadingDetails=true forever (stuck spinner). Not reproducible on the happy path (network served the details), but the missing catch is a real latent defect; severity medium.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to see records connected to the current one, so that I can follow conceptual threads through the archive.
expected_behavior: After fullRecord loads, entity data is fetched if not already loaded, then connection strength is computed against every non-social record (r.type!=='social') except the current one. Records with strength>0 are sorted by strength then prominenceScore and the top 6 kept. If none have entity connections, it falls back to up to 4 records sharing a category. Each related card shows date, a 'N shared entity/entities' chip (singular/plural), title, pub, and up to 4 shared-entity name chips with a '+N' overflow. Clicking a related card calls onSelectRecord(rel.id) to swap the open record. Section hidden when relatedWorks is empty.
test_notes: Open an article-type record with known entities and confirm a 'Related records' grid appears with shared-entity chips. Click a related card and confirm the modal swaps to that record. Open a sparse record to exercise the category fallback.
code_smell: findRelated loops calculateEntityConnectionStrength over the entire non-social record set on every open — O(N) synchronous work in an effect, potentially thousands of records.
notes: Related-records section rendered. Smell (O(N) synchronous calculateEntityConnectionStrength over the full non-social set in an effect) CONFIRMED in code (RecordModal.js:107 loops all candidates each open) — perf risk on large sets; modal still opened responsively in test.

user_story: As a reader, I want to page through records with buttons or arrow keys, so that I can browse sequentially without returning to the grid.
expected_behavior: Previous/Next footer buttons call onPrev/onNext and are disabled (opacity-30, cursor-not-allowed) when hasPrev/hasNext are false. ArrowLeft/ArrowRight keydown also fire onPrev/onNext but only when the corresponding hasPrev/hasNext is true. hasPrev/hasNext are derived by deriveNavFlags: hasPrev = index>0, hasNext = index>=0 && index<length-1. A deep-linked record filtered out of the list has index -1, so both flags are false and both buttons are correctly disabled (the #421 fix).
test_notes: Open a record and press ArrowLeft/ArrowRight; confirm it moves and the buttons grey out at the list ends. Deep-link (?record=) to a record that is filtered out, then confirm both nav buttons are disabled rather than clickable-but-inert.
code_smell: The keydown effect deps include onPrev/onNext/hasPrev/hasNext but not the record itself; handler captures handleClose from outer scope without listing it as a dep.
notes: Next button + ArrowLeft/ArrowRight keys all navigate; Previous disabled on first record (deriveNavFlags hasPrev=index>0). Smell (keydown effect omits record/handleClose from deps) does not manifest: handlers use latest hasPrev/hasNext which ARE in deps; nav stayed correct across 4 steps.

feature: Close modal (button, backdrop, ESC) with animation
user_story: As a reader, I want multiple ways to dismiss the modal, so that closing feels natural on any device.
expected_behavior: Clicking the X button, the dark backdrop, or pressing Escape calls handleClose, which sets isClosing=true (triggering a 300ms scale/opacity fade-out) and after a 300ms setTimeout calls onClose and resets isClosing. The inner panel has pointer-events-auto inside a pointer-events-none wrapper so only the panel and backdrop are interactive. ESC handling is gated on isOpen.
test_notes: Open a record, then close via X, via clicking the dimmed background, and via Escape. Confirm a short fade-out plays each time before the modal disappears.
code_smell: The 300ms setTimeout in handleClose is not cleared on unmount; closing then quickly navigating could fire onClose after teardown.
notes: All three close paths work; body overflow restored=true. Smell (300ms setTimeout in handleClose not cleared on unmount) is real but low-impact: close-then-immediate-teardown could fire onClose after unmount (no crash observed in normal close flows).

user_story: As a reader, I want to copy a shareable link to the exact record, so that I can send it to someone who lands on the same modal.
expected_behavior: The Share2 button builds `${origin}${pathname}?record=${record.id}` (no existing query/hash carried over), writes it to the clipboard via navigator.clipboard.writeText, and on success shows a 3-second toast 'Link copied to clipboard' (a stone-800 pill with a green CheckCircle that slides up and fades). Uses record (not fullRecord), so it works even before details finish loading.
test_notes: Open a record, click the share icon, confirm the toast appears and the clipboard holds a ?record=ID URL. Paste that URL in a fresh tab and confirm the same record opens.
code_smell: No catch on the clipboard promise — on browsers/contexts where clipboard write is denied (non-secure origin) nothing happens and no error toast shows; share URL discards any current hash route.
notes: Share button wrote "http://localhost:8000/index.html?record=dissertation-1986" and toast shown=true. Smell (no catch on clipboard write; share URL discards existing hash/query) CONFIRMED in code (RecordModal.js:169 builds origin+pathname+?record only, .then with no .catch) — on a denied clipboard nothing happens silently; low severity in secure context.

user_story: As a researcher, I want a one-click formatted citation, so that I can cite an archive record without hand-formatting it.
expected_behavior: The Quote button builds `${author} (${year}). "${title}". ${pub}. Retrieved from ${window.location.href}` from fullRecord and copies it to the clipboard, then shows the 3-second 'Citation copied to clipboard' toast. No-ops if fullRecord is null (details not yet loaded).
test_notes: Open a record, wait for details to load, click the quote icon, and paste to verify the citation string includes author, year, title, pub, and the current page URL.
code_smell: Retrieved-from URL is window.location.href (could already contain ?record= or other params); no clipboard-failure handling; year/pub/author can be undefined and render as literal 'undefined' in the citation.
notes: Citation written: "Jay Rosen (1986). "The Impossible Press: American Journalism and the Decline of Public Life". New York University (Ph.D. Dissertation). Retrieved from http://localhost:8000/index.html?record=dissertation-1986". Smell CONFIRMED: author/year/pub interpolated raw, so missing fields render literal "undefined"; Retrieved-from uses window.location.href (carries ?record=). undefinedPresent=false. No clipboard-failure handling.

user_story: As a reader, I want to click a category/tag/concept chip, so that I jump to the archive filtered by that term.
expected_behavior: Three TagGroups render: Thematic categories (onFilterCategory), Tags (onFilterSearch), Key concepts (onFilterSearch). Each chip is a button; clicking calls handleClose() then the relevant filter callback with the term. Chips are only interactive (hover/cursor styling) when a callback is provided; without one they render as static labels. A TagGroup with no tags renders null. The Era is shown as a single non-clickable dark badge.
test_notes: Open a record with categories and tags. Click a category chip and confirm the modal closes and the grid filters to that category; repeat for a tag and a concept (which both run a search).
code_smell: Categories filter and tags/concepts both labeled distinctly but tags and concepts call the same onFilterSearch path, so a concept and an identically-named tag are indistinguishable downstream.
notes: Clicked category "Journalism Education": modal closed=true, filtered list "677 records found". TagGroups present: categories=true tags=true concepts=true. Smell (tags & concepts share onFilterSearch so an identically-named tag/concept are indistinguishable downstream) CONFIRMED in code (App.js handleFilterSearch sets filters.search for both) — minor, both intentionally route to search; not a bug.

feature: External 'Read on' link with scheme sanitization
user_story: As a reader, I want a safe outbound link to the original source, so that I can read the full piece without exposure to malicious URLs.
expected_behavior: When url exists and is not '#', a 'Read on <pub>' link renders with target=_blank rel=noreferrer. The href is the stored record URL passed directly through sanitizeHref; no Bluesky-specific host rewrite is applied. sanitizeHref allows only http/https/mailto and scheme-less relative/protocol-relative URLs, returning '#' for anything else (e.g. javascript:, including obfuscated 'java\tscript:' that the URL parser collapses). Summary body text is linkified: bare http(s) URLs become target=_blank rel=noopener noreferrer links, other text rendered as-is.
test_notes: Open a record with a bsky.app source URL and confirm the link points at bsky.app, not embed.bsky.app. Manually craft a record with url='javascript:alert(1)' and confirm the link href is '#'. Open a record whose summary contains a URL and confirm it renders as a clickable link.
code_smell: Summary-body links built by linkifyText are not passed through sanitizeHref, but splitUrlsForLinkify only emits http(s) URLs, so the risk stays bounded unless the matcher changes.
notes: "Read on" link passes the stored record URL directly through sanitizeHref: bsky.app links stay on bsky.app and no Bluesky-specific rewrite is applied. SMELL REFUTED for the stated javascript: risk: utils/linkify.js splitUrlsForLinkify only matches https?:// URLs, so a "javascript:" token in summary text is rendered as plain text, never an <a href>. The summary linkify bypasses sanitizeHref, but it can only emit http/https hrefs.

user_story: As a reader, I want video records to play inline, so that I can watch without opening YouTube.
expected_behavior: If the url matches a YouTube id pattern, an aspect-video iframe loads https://www.youtube.com/embed/<id> with allowFullScreen. When a YouTube id is present the quote block is suppressed. Vimeo urls set isVideo (type label 'Video') but do not get an embedded player (only youtube ids are extracted).
test_notes: Open a record whose url is a youtube.com/watch?v= or youtu.be link and confirm the inline player renders and the quote block is hidden. Open a vimeo record and confirm it shows the 'Video' label but no embedded player.
code_smell: Vimeo is treated as video for the label but never embedded — inconsistent. The YouTube regex is broad and could mis-extract ids from non-watch URLs.
notes: YouTube embed iframe present=false on this record (only renders for matched youtube ids). Vimeo: label 'Video' but no embed — inconsistency CONFIRMED in code (only youtubeId is extracted; isVideo also true for vimeo). Behavior matches story; flagged as known design gap.

user_story: As a reader, I want the pull-quote shown only when it adds information, so that I am not shown the title twice.
expected_behavior: The italic blockquote renders only if there is no YouTube embed and a quote exists, AND the quote is meaningfully different from the title. It is suppressed when the trimmed title (>10 chars, trailing '...' stripped) equals the quote, the quote starts with the title, or the title starts with the leading slice of the quote. Otherwise the quote renders in a left-bordered blockquote.
test_notes: Open a record whose quote duplicates its title and confirm no blockquote shows; open one whose quote differs and confirm the blockquote appears.
code_smell: The prefix/substring comparison is heuristic and case-sensitive; a quote that differs only in case or punctuation from the title may still display redundantly.
notes: Quote blockquote present=true (suppressed when youtube embed exists or quote ~= title). Dedup heuristic is case-sensitive prefix/substring (RecordModal.js:269) — a case/punctuation-only difference could still show a near-duplicate quote; CONFIRMED as a heuristic limitation, low severity.

user_story: As a curator, I want auto-submitted records that haven't had a human pass flagged in the modal, so that I know the content is provisional.
expected_behavior: A 'needs review' amber badge (with a 'pending a human review pass' tooltip) renders under the title when recordNeedsReview(record) is true. The predicate is read from the core record (not displayRecord) deliberately, so a stale details.needsReview cannot overwrite a freshly flagged core record. recordNeedsReview returns true for boolean true or the trimmed/case-insensitive string 'true', false for everything else (false, '', other strings, null, absent).
test_notes: No flagged records ship in production yet; set needsReview=true (or 'true') on a record fixture and confirm the amber badge appears. Confirm needsReview='false' or absent shows no badge.
notes: Badge absent on first record (depends on record flag). Render path wired; predicate reads core record (RecordModal.js:232 uses recordNeedsReview(record), not displayRecord) — matches story intent.

user_story: As a reader, I want a threaded social-media post rendered in reading order with reply nesting, so that I can follow a Bluesky conversation inside the archive.
expected_behavior: Inside RecordModal, if the record id starts with 'THREAD-' and thread_data exists, ThreadModal renders instead of the plain summary. It shows a stats bar (total_posts posts, max_depth levels deep, 'Bluesky thread') and a scrollable (max-h-600px) list of posts. Each post shows 'Post number/totalPosts', a locale-formatted date (falls back to the raw string on parse error), content (whitespace-pre-wrap, URLs linkified) or '[No content]' when empty, and a 'View on Bluesky' link. Reply depth sets a left margin (min(depth,5)*16px) and a colored left border by depth (sky/green/amber/pink for 0/1/2/3+). If thread_data or thread_data.posts is missing, it logs a diagnostic and renders 'Thread data not available'.
test_notes: Open a THREAD- record with thread_data and confirm posts render nested with depth colors, the stats bar counts, and Bluesky links. Open a THREAD- record whose thread_data is missing/unparsed and confirm the 'Thread data not available' message.
code_smell: ThreadModal ships its own linkify regex (separate from utils/linkify.js) using a stateful urlPattern.test() with manual lastIndex reset — the documented bug class linkify.js was created to avoid. A console.log diagnostic remains in production code.
notes: Thread THREAD-00009: viewer=true stats(posts/levels/Bluesky)=true. Smell CONFIRMED: ThreadModal ships its own stateful-regex linkify (urlPattern.test with manual lastIndex reset — the exact bug class utils/linkify.js exists to avoid) and keeps a console.log diagnostic (ThreadModal.js:107). Functional here but a maintenance/latent-bug smell.

user_story: As a reader, I want each thread post's outbound link to be safe and pointed at Bluesky, so that I can view the original post.
expected_behavior: Each post's 'View on Bluesky' href is the stored post URL passed directly through sanitizeHref (http/https/mailto/relative allowed, else '#'); no Bluesky-specific host rewrite is applied. Opens target=_blank rel=noopener noreferrer.
test_notes: In an open thread, hover a 'View on Bluesky' link and confirm it points at bsky.app, not embed.bsky.app. Confirm a malformed post url collapses to '#'.
notes: "View on Bluesky" hrefs pass the stored post URL directly through sanitizeHref: bsky.app links stay on bsky.app, target=_blank and rel=noopener noreferrer are preserved, and javascript: hrefs are rejected.

user_story: As a reader of the dissertation, I want a node's details to slide in from the side, so that I can read its summary, quote, concepts, and figures without losing the mind map.
expected_behavior: A right-edge panel (full width on mobile, 420px on >=sm, capped at calc(100vw-16px)) slides in/out via translate based on isOpen. role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-labelledby=detail-panel-title. On open the close button is focused after a 100ms delay; Escape closes (listener only attached while open). On mobile a semi-transparent backdrop (sm:hidden) closes on click. The last node is retained in displayNode so the panel can animate out with content (never cleared to null on close). Header shows a TYPE_LABELS label (root/intro/part/chapter/conclusion/concept/figure, else 'Section'). Body conditionally shows subtitle, page reference (pageRef or 'Pages start[-end|+]'), pull quote, summary, key concepts (violet chips), key figures (green chips). If none of summary/pullQuote/keyConcepts/keyFigures exist, shows a 'Detailed content coming soon' empty state. Renders null only if a node has never been set.
test_notes: On #dissertation, click a mind-map node and confirm the panel slides in with the right label and sections. Press Escape and click outside (mobile width) to close. Click a node with no detail fields and confirm the 'coming soon' state.
code_smell: displayNode is intentionally never cleared, so after closing, the stale panel content remains mounted (just translated offscreen) and is still in the a11y tree until a new node replaces it.
notes: DetailPanel opened on node click: role=dialog aria-modal=true on-screen=true close-btn=true. After ESC the panel stays MOUNTED and translates off-screen (afterEsc.stillMounted=true, offScreen=true). SMELL CONFIRMED: displayNode is intentionally never cleared (DetailPanel.js:27), so stale panel content remains in the a11y tree (translated offscreen but still in DOM, aria-modal=true) until a new node replaces it — a real accessibility nit.

user_story: As a reader, I want a menu of ways to explore the dissertation and data, so that I can pick mind map, FAQ, reader, or data viz.
expected_behavior: A centered dialog (z-[100], role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-labelledby) over a blurred backdrop. Body scroll locked while open and restored on close/unmount. Close button focused 100ms after open; Escape closes; clicking the backdrop (target===currentTarget) closes. Two sections: Dissertation Tools (Mind Map in-page action, FAQ link, Dissertation Reader link [beta]) and Data Tools (Data Visualization link [beta]). Each card is a button; 'beta' cards show an amber Beta pill. Clicking an action tool calls onSelectTool(action) then onClose; clicking a link tool navigates via window.location.href = tool.href. Footer explains the Beta marker. Renders null when closed.
test_notes: Trigger the tools modal, confirm focus lands on the close button, Escape and backdrop-click both close it, the Mind Map card runs the in-page action and closes, and link cards navigate to the dissertation/faq/reader/dataviz URLs.
code_smell: Tool hrefs are hardcoded absolute production paths ('/j/rosen-archive/...'), so on localhost or a different deploy path the FAQ/reader/dataviz links 404. firstToolRef is wired but never used for focus.
errors_found: Link-tool hrefs are hardcoded to production /j/rosen-archive/... and 404 on localhost/preview: /j/rosen-archive/dissertation/faq/=404, /j/rosen-archive/dissertation/reader/=404, /j/rosen-archive/tools/active/dataviz/dataviz.html=404
fix_applied: Fixed at source: added resolveSitePath()/getSiteRoot()/SITE_ROOT to pathResolver.js and routed ToolsModal.js tool hrefs (faq/reader/dataviz) through it. Links now resolve in local, GitHub Pages, and production instead of only the hardcoded /j/rosen-archive prod path.
notes: ToolsModal: role=dialog z=100 sections(diss=true,data=true) cards(MindMap=true,FAQ=true,Reader=true,DataViz=true) Beta=true, ESC-close=true, body overflow="hidden". SMELL: hrefs hardcoded to /j/rosen-archive/... (ToolsModal.js:22-41) — confirmed below via HTTP probe; firstToolRef wired but unused for focus (close button gets focus instead). CONFIRMED: all ToolsModal link hrefs 404 on localhost (/j/rosen-archive/dissertation/faq/=404, /j/rosen-archive/dissertation/reader/=404, /j/rosen-archive/tools/active/dataviz/dataviz.html=404) — FAQ/Reader/DataViz links are dead in local dev / any non-/j/rosen-archive deploy. | RETEST: faq=/dissertation/faq/(200) reader=/dissertation/reader/(200) dataviz=/tools/active/dataviz/dataviz.html(200)

user_story: As a first-time visitor, I want a one-time intro to the archive, so that I understand what it is before I start browsing.
expected_behavior: On mount it reads localStorage 'jrda_visited'; if absent, the modal becomes visible (full-screen dark overlay, z-[70]). It introduces the archive with three feature hints (browse records, explore connections, read the dissertation). Clicking 'Enter archive' sets localStorage 'jrda_visited'='true' and hides the modal. Once visited, it never shows again. No close button other than the Enter button, and no Escape handler.
test_notes: Clear localStorage key jrda_visited and reload to see the modal; click 'Enter archive' and reload to confirm it does not reappear. Confirm Escape does NOT dismiss it.
code_smell: No Escape/backdrop dismissal and no role=dialog/aria-modal — the only exit is the single button; a user who blocks localStorage would see it on every load.
notes: First visit showed welcome modal=true; Enter set jrda_visited="true" and hid it; second visit suppressed=true. SMELL CONFIRMED: no role=dialog/aria-modal, no ESC/backdrop dismissal (only the Enter button); a localStorage-blocked browser would see it every load. Functional but an a11y/edge-case gap.

user_story: As a returning visitor, I want to dismiss the launch announcement, so that it doesn't take space on every visit.
expected_behavior: Starts hidden (dismissed=true) to avoid a flash, then on mount reads localStorage 'jrda_announce_banner_dismissed'; if not set, the banner shows (sky-tinted bar announcing public availability and '25,000+ records'). Clicking the X sets dismissed=true and persists the localStorage flag so it stays hidden on future loads. Renders null when dismissed.
test_notes: Clear localStorage key jrda_announce_banner_dismissed and reload to see the banner; click the X and reload to confirm it stays gone.
code_smell: Hardcoded '25,000+ records' copy can drift from the actual record count; no aria-live so the banner's appearance isn't announced.
notes: Banner shown on fresh state=true, X set flag="true" and hid it; reload kept hidden=true. SMELL: hardcoded "25,000+ records" (present=true) can drift from the real ~30,700-record total; no aria-live so the banner is not announced. Copy-drift + a11y nit, low severity.

user_story: As a visitor waiting for the archive to load, I want a branded loading screen, so that the wait feels intentional and on-theme.
expected_behavior: Shows a pulsing BookOpen in a spinning ring, a quote from a fixed set of 9 dissertation quotes attributed to 'The Impossible Press, <source>', three bouncing dots, 'Loading archive...', and a 'Records are cached for faster loading next time' tip. The starting quote is random; every 4 seconds it fades out (300ms), advances to the next quote (wrapping), and fades back in. Interval is cleared on unmount.
test_notes: Load the archive cold (or throttle the network) and confirm the quote rotates every ~4s with a fade, the spinner animates, and the tip text shows.
code_smell: Quotes are hardcoded and duplicated from dissertationData rather than sourced from it, risking drift from the verified citations.
notes: LoadingQuotes captured during throttled cold load: "Loading archive..."/tip=true, "The Impossible Press, <source>" cite=true. SMELL: the 9 quotes are hardcoded in LoadingQuotes.js (duplicated from dissertationData, risk of drift from verified citations) — confirmed by source; not a runtime failure. Rotation/random-start/cleanup are in-source per story.

user_story: As a reader following a shared link, I want ?record=ID to open that record directly, so that links land on the exact item.
expected_behavior: parseRecordId reads the 'record' query param from any search string ('?record=ID', 'record=ID', or a full search with other params), returning the id or null when absent or present-but-empty (an empty id must not open a modal). setRecordParam sets ?record= for a truthy id and deletes it for any falsy id (null/undefined/''), returning the same params for chaining. Both router.js and App.js delegate here so the read and the set/delete rule have a single definition. A record id outside the current filtered list still opens (looked up in the full set) but yields disabled prev/next via deriveNavFlags.
test_notes: Open a record and confirm the URL gains ?record=ID; close it and confirm the param is removed. Load a URL with ?record= (empty) and confirm no modal opens. Load ?record=<id-not-in-current-filter> and confirm the modal opens with disabled nav.
code_smell: parseRecordId does not validate that the id corresponds to a real record — a ?record=garbage value is passed downstream and relies on the lookup returning nothing.
notes: Cold ?record=dissertation-1986 opened modal; URL kept the param; close deleted it (setRecordParam delete branch); ?record=GARBAGE opened no modal (lookup misses -> record null -> RecordModal returns null). Smell (parseRecordId does not validate the id is real) CONFIRMED but harmless — the downstream lookup returning nothing is the intended guard, verified live.

user_story: As a user who hits a problem, I want a one-click bug report that already includes my context, so that I can report without typing my page URL, version, or user agent.
expected_behavior: openBugReport reads live context at click time and opens, in a new tab (noopener,noreferrer), a github.com new-issue URL prefilled via query params that map to bug_report.yml field ids: page-context=window.location.href (so any open ?record= is captured), archive-version=ARCHIVE_VERSION (the ?v= cache-buster this module was imported with, else 'unknown'), browser=navigator.userAgent, plus template=bug_report.yml and labels=bug,user-report. buildBugReportUrl is pure (context passed in) for testing.
test_notes: Click the report-a-bug control and confirm a new tab opens GitHub's new-issue form with Page, Archive version, and Browser fields prefilled. Open a record first and confirm the page-context includes ?record=ID.
code_smell: The page-context/archive-version/browser query keys must stay in sync with the template field ids by hand; a rename in bug_report.yml silently drops the prefill (verified matching as of this audit).
notes: Report-a-bug opened a new tab with prefilled URL. template/labels/page-context/archive-version/browser params all present; feat="noopener,noreferrer". page-context captured the open ?record= deep link=true. Smell (query keys must hand-match bug_report.yml field ids) noted; matching verified as of audit. URL: https://github.com/jamditis/rosen-frontend/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml&labels=bug%2Cuser-report&page-context=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A8000%2Findex.html%3...

feature: Entity data loading and loading state
user_story: As a researcher, I want the entity index to load when I open #entities, so that I can browse extracted people, organizations, and concepts.
expected_behavior: On mount, EntityBrowser calls fetchEntitiesData() and shows a centered spinner with the text 'Loading entity data...' while loading is true. When the fetch resolves with data.entities, the list renders; data.recordEntityMap is stored for co-occurrence math. If the fetch fails, archiveService returns { entities: [], recordEntityMap: {} }, so the spinner clears and the browser renders with zero entities (All (0) chip, empty grid, 'Showing 0 of 0 entities') rather than an error. Subsequent visits use the in-memory entitiesCache.
test_notes: Open #entities. Confirm the spinner appears briefly, then the chip row and entity grid render. Throttle/block /data/archive-entities.json in devtools and reload to confirm it degrades to an empty list with no thrown error.
code_smell: A failed fetch is swallowed into an empty-result object, so the user sees a silent empty state indistinguishable from 'no entities exist' rather than any retry or error message.
notes: Spinner cleared, list rendered. All (7379); 100 of 7379 shown. Failed-fetch-swallowed-to-empty smell is real in code (catch returns {entities:[]}) but not reproducible against a healthy server; confirmed by source review.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to filter entities by type (People, Organizations, Concepts, etc.), so that I can narrow the list to one category.
expected_behavior: A chip row renders an 'All (N)' chip (N = total entities) plus one chip per type from ENTITY_TYPE_CONFIG that has count > 0; each shows its icon, label, and per-type count. Clicking a type chip filters the grid to that type and highlights the chip in the type's color; clicking the active chip again toggles the filter off (back to All). Clicking 'All' clears the type filter. Types with zero entities render no chip. Changing the type resets the display limit to 100.
test_notes: Open #entities, click 'People' — grid shows only Person entities and chip turns blue. Click it again to deselect. Confirm a type with no entities (e.g. Event/Location if absent) shows no chip.
code_smell: Type counts (typeCounts) are computed from the raw entities array, so a type chip can be hidden even when ENTITY_TYPE_CONFIG defines it; this is intended but means the visible type set silently depends on the data file.
notes: 6 type chips render with counts (People (2668), Organizations (1659), Concepts (1322), Works (997), Events (466), Locations (267)). Clicking filters to the type count; clicking active chip toggles back to All. Counts are data-driven (typeCounts from entities) as the smell describes — intended behavior.

feature: Search entities by name or role
user_story: As a researcher, I want to type a query and have the entity list filter live, so that I can find a specific person or concept quickly.
expected_behavior: Typing in the search box (onInput) filters entities whose normalized name OR normalized role contains the normalized term (normalizeForSearch handles case/diacritics). Filtering combines with the active type filter and chosen sort. A clear (X) button appears only when searchTerm is non-empty and empties the field on click. Changing the search term resets the display limit to 100. An empty result set renders an empty grid and 'Showing 0 of 0 entities' (no dedicated 'no matches' message).
test_notes: Open #entities, type 'lippmann' — list narrows. Type gibberish to confirm an empty grid plus 'Showing 0 of 0'. Click the X to clear. Combine search with a type chip to confirm both apply.
code_smell: No explicit 'no results found' empty state for search; the user only sees a blank grid and a count of 0, which reads as a glitch.
errors_found: No-match search shows "Showing 0 of 0 entities" with no dedicated empty-state message (hasNoResultsMsg=false).
notes: Search narrows (7379->20 for 'rosen'); clear (X) empties the field. Confirmed smell: an empty result set renders a blank grid + count of 0, no "no results found" message. Minor UX gap, behaves as coded.

user_story: As a researcher, I want to sort entities by mentions, prominence, or alphabetically, so that I can surface the most significant entities first.
expected_behavior: A select offers 'Most mentioned' (default, sorts by totalMentions desc, falling back to 1), 'Highest prominence' (prominence desc, falling back to 0), and 'Alphabetical' (name localeCompare asc). Changing sort re-orders the grid immediately and resets the display limit to 100. Sort applies after type and search filtering.
test_notes: Open #entities, switch the sort dropdown between the three options and confirm the first cards change order. With 'Alphabetical', confirm A-Z ordering.

feature: Pan the canvas (drag, touch, arrow keys)

user_story: As a researcher, I want entity-to-record and record-to-entity lookups to be accurate, so that the records and co-occurrences I see actually reflect the archive.
expected_behavior: EntityBrowser wires getRecordsByEntity/getEntityById from archiveService.js, whose maps are built in buildEntityMaps from each record's relatedIds. recordEntityMap (record id -> entity ids) is also returned to the browser for the co-occurrence tally. getRecordsByEntity returns an array of record IDs (deduplicated via a Set) for an entity, or an empty array when the entity has no relationships. The separate entityIndex.js factory provides a frozen, sorted-by-prominence Query (entitiesOf, recordsOf, shared, strength, types) that is the tested pure projection of the same relationships.
test_notes: Open #entities, pick an entity and verify the records listed in the panel genuinely reference that entity by opening one. Cross-check the panel's '<n> records' against the card's mention count. There is no direct UI surface for entityIndex.js — it is exercised by tests/entity-index.test.js.
code_smell: The UI consumes archiveService.js's hand-rolled entity maps while entityIndex.js (the frozen, tested, prominence-sorted projection) is not wired into EntityBrowser, so two parallel implementations of the same relationship logic can drift; entityIndex sorts results by prominence whereas the browser sorts records by date and co-entities by count.
errors_found: EntityBrowser imports getRecordsByEntity/getEntityById from archiveService.js, NOT from entityIndex.js (frozen prominence-sorted projection). Two parallel relationship implementations coexist and can drift.
fix_applied: EntityBrowser uses archiveService getRecordsByEntity/getEntityById, not the frozen entityIndex.js projection. Both are runtime-correct; the parallel implementations are a drift risk, not an error. Deferred (pick one source of truth later).
notes: Confirmed smell via source: archiveService.buildEntityMaps powers the UI; entityIndex.js (the tested pure projection) is wired into tests only, not the browser. Relationships resolve correctly at runtime (records + co-occurrence render), so functionally OK today, but the duplication is real (browser sorts records by date / co-entities by count; entityIndex sorts by prominence). | RETEST: not fixed (deferred: runtime-correct, parallel impls); Phase 2 finding stands.

Confirmed smell: header subtitle "Powered by sql.js (SQLite in your browser)" present (true) but the default view renders entirely from prebuilt JSON aggregates and never touches SQLite — misleading.

user_story: As a non-technical visitor, I want to build database queries by completing plain-English sentences with dropdowns and inputs, so that I can explore the archive without knowing SQL.

feature: Web Storage quota handling and legacy sessionStorage cleanup
user_story: As a heavy user whose browser storage is nearly full, I want caching to fail gracefully, so that the archive keeps working when storage is exhausted.

On a QuotaExceededError it clears all archive_* keys via clearArchiveCache() and retries once; if it still fails it logs 'Cache disabled: browser storage is full' and continues without caching. getCachedData reads a legacy sessionStorage entry before localStorage so older builds' caches expire cleanly, and evicts entries that mismatch CACHE_VERSION or exceed the 30-min TTL. clearArchiveCache also fire-and-forget clears the IndexedDB core store.

Confirm archive_* keys are cleared on quota error. Set jrda_debug and observe cache read/eviction behavior on TTL/version mismatch (manually edit a cached entry's version).

Quota/eviction/TTL branches are internal and not reliably triggerable in headless chromium without synthetic quota pressure: covered by unit suite tests/session-cache-overflow.test.js + tests/idb-cache.test.js.
